target.title: fix(gateway): reject profile imports and host-local routes in browser proxy
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a write-scoped operator could invoke persistent browser profile imports or query host-local routes (such as system profiles) on paired nodes via `browser.proxy`. This could allow unauthorized profile mutations or leak Keychain/browser profile metadata from remote nodes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligns the gateway's browser proxy validation with the node host's request policy:
1. Updated `isPersistentBrowserProxyMutation` in `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts` to include `/profiles/import`.
2. Added `isBrowserProxyHostLocalRoute` and `isForbiddenBrowserProxyHostLocalRoute` check functions to detect host-local routes like `/system-profiles`, `/system-profile-import/status`, and `/system-profile-import/dismiss` at the gateway layer.
3. Rejects these requests in the gateway before forwarding them, failing fast with `ErrorCodes.INVALID_REQUEST`.

## User Impact

Improves security and isolation of paired nodes by ensuring write-scoped operators cannot bypass mutation checks or retrieve host-local keychain/profile data from remote nodes via browser proxy.

## Evidence

Added new unit/integration tests in `src/gateway/server.node-invoke-approval-bypass.test.ts` to verify the gateway blocks `/profiles/import` and `/system-profiles` requests via `browser.proxy`.

### Test Results
Running Vitest confirms the added tests pass successfully:

target.title: feat(discord): show subagent progress
target.body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in Discord-scoped sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message, including count reactions, durable failure marker behavior, and typing keepalive while tracked work is active.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord users currently have little visible feedback when an assistant turn delegates work to tracked sub-agents. Long-running turns can look idle after the initial message even though background sub-agents are still running, and a sub-agent failure is not visible on the original Discord message.

Discord also cannot represent concurrent work by adding the same emoji reaction multiple times from the same bot/user, so progress needs a count-based reaction model instead of repeated identical reactions.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Discord users get immediate, lightweight progress feedback during delegated work without waiting for the final assistant reply:

- `1️⃣`, `2️⃣`, etc. show the current active tracked sub-agent count for the turn
- the count reaction is replaced as the active count changes
- the count reaction disappears when no tracked sub-agents remain active
- `🔴` remains if any tracked sub-agent ends with a non-OK outcome
- typing stays active while tracked sub-agents are still running

Operators can configure the behavior with `channels.discord.subagentProgress`, including reaction progress, count emoji, failure emoji, typing keepalive, interval, and max-duration TTL.

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

## Linked Context

No linked issues or external context were listed in the current PR body.

## What Changes

This PR adds Discord-scoped, best-effort sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message. The feature is opt-in with `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`.

When enabled:

- one configurable count reaction shows the number of currently active tracked sub-agents (`1️⃣` … `🔟` by default)
- count changes replace the previous count reaction instead of accumulating multiple ordinal reactions
- zero active tracked sub-agents removes the count reaction
- any non-OK completion leaves a durable configurable failure marker (`🔴` by default)
- Discord typing is kept alive independently while tracked sub-agents remain active, then stops when all tracked work finishes or the safety TTL expires

The implementation threads the source Discord message id through native `sessions_spawn`, tracked ACP spawn, requester origin metadata, and internal Discord progress hook handling so the Discord extension can target the correct parent message. Non-Discord callers and callers without a source message id keep existing behavior.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds source/current message id propagation through delivery context and `sessions_spawn` tool context.
- Carries that id into native sub-agent spawn and tracked ACP registration.
- Keeps public plugin hook/requester metadata narrow while the Discord extension uses an internal Discord-only event shape for source-message progress targeting.
- Emits progress cleanup at run completion even when ordinary `subagent_ended` delivery is deferred.
- Adds a Discord progress tracker keyed by account id, parent channel id, typing/thread target id, and source message id to avoid thread collisions.
- Tracks active run ids and derives the displayed count from current active set size.
- Replaces the displayed count reaction when the active count changes, removes it at zero, and caps counts above the configured emoji list to the final configured emoji.
- Uses `unref` on typing timers where supported so keepalive intervals do not keep Node alive.
- Updates Discord config schema, exported config types, UI hints, generated channel config metadata, and docs.

## Tests / Verification

Focused validation and static/config/docs gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `20a11bf331429ed2fd521636910b4aa07c5dcc24`
- Current PR head: `0f0ea76085d4ddc271aa25bab129f9c518f95992`
- Re-squashed to one commit on the common base; pushed with `--force-with-lease`.
- Removed invalid/unnecessary delivered-text visibility experiment from `d17f593b4d4428f6ba7318f55eb40d76c3932094`; legitimate Discord sub-agent progress behavior remains.

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live Discord proof for source-message progress behavior, not only tests. The requested coverage was: count reaction add/replace/remove behavior, normal channel context, thread/forum context, concurrent tracked sub-agents, typing keepalive while tracked work is active, typing stop/drain and TTL behavior, and durable failure-marker behavior after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle.

The live proof below covers those requested behaviors: normal channel success, thread-bound success, concurrent count replacement/increment/decrement/clear, typing keepalive/stop plus TTL guard logs, and a durable failure marker retained on the original source message after non-OK lifecycle. Private host/path/token/session/network values are redacted; Discord IDs/timestamps shown are included only where they are needed to tie the proof to the source-message behavior.

### Real / Live Behavior Proof

Live Discord API proof was run from the installed PR stack on Dev-01 using `OpenClaw 2026.6.10-beta.1` at local HEAD `f15c88bd6f9 stack: combine beta memory slots and Discord progress`, with:

- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.reactions.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.typing.enabled=true`

Observed live behavior in Discord:

- **Normal channel success:** a Discord-originated parent turn spawned a tracked sub-agent run (`8c6dbfa0-e021-4c3a-9992-328de22caa13`). The source Discord message showed the active count reaction while the child was running, typing stayed active during child work, and the count reaction was removed after the child completed. Child proof line: `NORMAL_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:48:33Z`.
- **Thread-bound success:** a thread-bound Discord sub-agent run (`01fa6443-4fc1-409d-9cf3-969ce433edbd`) completed successfully while progress was shown from the Discord parent context. Child proof line: `THREAD_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:49:50Z`.
- **Concurrent count replacement:** two overlapping tracked sub-agent runs (`4b2701ef-85b0-41d5-a87f-f72924e21869` and `9a5b1e70-5b3b-4820-bb5f-cb6cb7b2a926`) exercised count add/replace/remove behavior. The Discord source message count reaction incremented while both children were active, decremented as the first child completed, and cleared after the second child completed. Child proof lines: `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_2_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:23Z` and `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_3_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:36Z`.
- **Typing keepalive/stop:** Discord typing was visible while tracked sub-agents were active and stopped after tracked work drained. Earlier long-running proof passes also hit the configured typing safety TTL, with gateway logs showing `[typing] TTL exceeded (60000ms), auto-stopping typing indicator`, confirming the timeout guard executes.

Additional observation: after the final child drains, there can be a brief visual gap before the parent posts its final reconciliation response. That appears to be parent-yield lifecycle behavior rather than this PR's sub-agent progress tracker; it is being tracked separately as a follow-up investigation and is not treated as a blocker for this PR.

Additional durable failure-marker proof was captured from a real Discord source message after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle:

- **Failure marker:** source message `1518528276031602788` in Discord channel `1507934992699756645` retained the configured durable failure reaction `🔴` with count `1` and `me: true` after the non-OK sub-agent lifecycle. The source message timestamp was `2026-06-22T08:09:13.897Z`. A later follow-up heartbeat at `2026-06-22T08:29:48.355Z` reported a separate verification pass, confirming the red marker was left on the original source message rather than being ordinary final text delivery.

Redacted observation:

```json
{
  "channel_id": "1507934992699756645",
  "message_id": "1518528276031602788",
  "timestampUtc": "2026-06-22T08:09:13.897Z",
  "content": "Extensively check over the branch end-to-end against the recommended fix and prior investigation/research to ensure everything is clean, finalized, and polished.",
  "reactions": [
    {
      "emoji": { "name": "🔴" },
      "count": 1,
      "me": true
    }
  ]
}
```

## Compatibility and Risk

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

target.title: fix: deleting a session leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk
target.body:
Closes [#89200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89200)

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and tests were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and validated it against a live deployment's session store.

## What Problem This Solves

Session trajectory artifacts (`.trajectory.jsonl` + `.trajectory-path.json`) were handled inconsistently, and destructively, across the session lifecycle:

1. **Delete** (dashboard / `sessions.delete` RPC) archived the transcript but left the trajectory pair orphaned on disk forever (the original [#89200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89200) defect).
2. **Reset paths** either deleted the trajectory outright (destroying the forensic tool-call record, flagged as a P1 by the automated review on this PR) or left it at its live name to be misclassified later.
3. The **typed `/new` and `/reset`** commands (and the implicit daily/idle rollover) went through a code path with no trajectory handling at all, so fixes applied to the other reset doors never reached the path users actually type.

## What This Change Does

One consistent model: **trajectory artifacts shadow their transcript**. Whenever a session's transcript is archived with a `.reset.<ts>` or `.deleted.<ts>` suffix, the trajectory runtime file and pointer are renamed with the byte-identical suffix in the same operation (shared `nowMs`), never unlinked:

- A `TrajectoryArtifactDisposal` union threads the disposal mode through the cleanup helpers: `{ mode: "tombstone", reason, nowMs }` for user-visible lifecycle events, with rename-in-place semantics under the same `withTrajectoryPathLock` retire turn.
- All three lifecycle doors are coupled: `deleteSessionEntryLifecycle` (delete), `resetSessionEntryLifecycle` (dashboard New Session button), and the typed-command rollover path `initSessionState` → `commitReplySessionInitialization`, plus the internal self-heal path `persistSessionResetLifecycle`.
- The referenced-sessions guard snapshot is taken **inside the locked store mutator** (`referencedSessionIdsAtSwap`), closing a race where an unlocked re-read after two await points could see a concurrent writer's row and silently skip the tombstone.
- **External trajectory directories** (`OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR`): the pair is tombstoned in place only under proven ownership (registry-owned, or the session's own pointer file names the target); unproven files in an operator-configured directory are left untouched. The retention sweep follows tombstone directories, so aging works there too.
- **No new retention code.** Tombstoned trajectories reuse the existing `.reset.<ts>` / `.deleted.<ts>` suffix conventions and age out with the existing archived-transcript sweep.

## Why rename instead of delete on reset

No merged commit or confirmed-maintainer comment currently states reset-vs-trajectory policy explicitly, but the record strongly and repeatedly converges on one answer: reset must preserve trajectory records via rename/archive, never delete them outright. This is proposed directly in [#90707](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90707) (with a concrete forensics-loss incident as motivation), implemented the same way in the still-open [#94593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94593) (after two prior closed-unmerged attempts at the identical shape, [#93319](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93319) and [#94895](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94895)), echoed by the broader "never `rm` a session file, only move/rename" position in [#56609](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/56609), and most directly, flagged as a P1 blocker on this very branch by the automated reviewer, which asked explicitly to "preserve or archive pre-reset trajectories instead of deleting them." This PR's tombstone-rename on the runner-driven `/reset` path is our attempt to satisfy that converging intent without waiting on #94593 to land, since the two changes touch adjacent but distinct code paths (delete-lifecycle cleanup vs. the shared reset-archive helper) and reconciling them is better done as a maintainer-guided follow-up than by blocking this fix on an unrelated open PR.

## Evidence

Test gates on the final head: `session-accessor.test.ts` 73/73, `session.test.ts` 143/143, adjacent lifecycle suites 24/24 (240 total), typecheck (`tsgo:core` + `tsgo:core:test`) clean, oxlint/oxfmt clean. Every fix commit is red-proven: the concurrent-writer race test and the entry-level typed-`/reset` test (entering through `initSessionState`, not the inner function) each fail against the pre-fix code exactly as observed live and pass after.

Live validation on a v2026.6.10 production deployment (session ids redacted):

```
typed /reset:
  <sid-A>.jsonl.reset.2026-07-11T16-45-15.346Z
  <sid-A>.trajectory.jsonl.reset.2026-07-11T16-45-15.346Z
  <sid-A>.trajectory-path.json.reset.2026-07-11T16-45-15.346Z

dashboard delete: same trio shape with .deleted.<ts>, session key removed, clean re-mint on next message

typed /new with OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR set (trajectory lives outside the sessions dir):
  sessions dir:  <sid-B>.jsonl.reset.<ts>  +  <sid-B>.trajectory-path.json.reset.<ts>
  external dir:  <sid-B>.jsonl.reset.<ts>   (renamed in place, same timestamp)
```

## Scope notes

- `applySessionEntryLifecycleMutation` (the batched background-maintenance mutation used by the session reaper, cleanup service, and heartbeat runner) is deliberately not touched: its removed-session cleanup already routes through the trajectory-coupled maintenance helpers, and unreferenced pairs are reclaimed by the age-based prune, which is the correct model for background reaping (no user action to timestamp-couple to).
- [#94593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94593) partially overlaps on intent (reset-time preservation) but implements it in the shared reset-archive helper; this PR covers the delete lifecycle and the typed-command rollover door. If #94593 lands first we are happy to rebase and drop any overlap, and vice versa.

## User Impact

Deleting or resetting a session, from any surface, now leaves a complete archived trio with one shared timestamp instead of orphaned or destroyed trajectory files. Post-incident forensics of tool calls survives resets. Existing retention behavior and bounds are unchanged.

target.title: fix: deleting a session leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk
target.body:
Closes [#89200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89200)

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and tests were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and validated it against a live deployment's session store.

## What Problem This Solves

Session trajectory artifacts (`.trajectory.jsonl` + `.trajectory-path.json`) were handled inconsistently, and destructively, across the session lifecycle:

1. **Delete** (dashboard / `sessions.delete` RPC) archived the transcript but left the trajectory pair orphaned on disk forever (the original [#89200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89200) defect).
2. **Reset paths** either deleted the trajectory outright (destroying the forensic tool-call record, flagged as a P1 by the automated review on this PR) or left it at its live name to be misclassified later.
3. The **typed `/new` and `/reset`** commands (and the implicit daily/idle rollover) went through a code path with no trajectory handling at all, so fixes applied to the other reset doors never reached the path users actually type.

## What This Change Does

One consistent model: **trajectory artifacts shadow their transcript**. Whenever a session's transcript is archived with a `.reset.<ts>` or `.deleted.<ts>` suffix, the trajectory runtime file and pointer are renamed with the byte-identical suffix in the same operation (shared `nowMs`), never unlinked:

- A `TrajectoryArtifactDisposal` union threads the disposal mode through the cleanup helpers: `{ mode: "tombstone", reason, nowMs }` for user-visible lifecycle events, with rename-in-place semantics under the same `withTrajectoryPathLock` retire turn.
- All three lifecycle doors are coupled: `deleteSessionEntryLifecycle` (delete), `resetSessionEntryLifecycle` (dashboard New Session button), and the typed-command rollover path `initSessionState` → `commitReplySessionInitialization`, plus the internal self-heal path `persistSessionResetLifecycle`.
- The referenced-sessions guard snapshot is taken **inside the locked store mutator** (`referencedSessionIdsAtSwap`), closing a race where an unlocked re-read after two await points could see a concurrent writer's row and silently skip the tombstone.
- **External trajectory directories** (`OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR`): the pair is tombstoned in place only under proven ownership (registry-owned, or the session's own pointer file names the target); unproven files in an operator-configured directory are left untouched. The retention sweep follows tombstone directories, so aging works there too.
- **No new retention code.** Tombstoned trajectories reuse the existing `.reset.<ts>` / `.deleted.<ts>` suffix conventions and age out with the existing archived-transcript sweep.

## Why rename instead of delete on reset

No merged commit or confirmed-maintainer comment currently states reset-vs-trajectory policy explicitly, but the record strongly and repeatedly converges on one answer: reset must preserve trajectory records via rename/archive, never delete them outright. This is proposed directly in [#90707](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90707) (with a concrete forensics-loss incident as motivation), implemented the same way in the still-open [#94593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94593) (after two prior closed-unmerged attempts at the identical shape, [#93319](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93319) and [#94895](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94895)), echoed by the broader "never `rm` a session file, only move/rename" position in [#56609](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/56609), and most directly, flagged as a P1 blocker on this very branch by the automated reviewer, which asked explicitly to "preserve or archive pre-reset trajectories instead of deleting them." This PR's tombstone-rename on the runner-driven `/reset` path is our attempt to satisfy that converging intent without waiting on #94593 to land, since the two changes touch adjacent but distinct code paths (delete-lifecycle cleanup vs. the shared reset-archive helper) and reconciling them is better done as a maintainer-guided follow-up than by blocking this fix on an unrelated open PR.

## Evidence

Test gates on the final head: `session-accessor.test.ts` 73/73, `session.test.ts` 143/143, adjacent lifecycle suites 24/24 (240 total), typecheck (`tsgo:core` + `tsgo:core:test`) clean, oxlint/oxfmt clean. Every fix commit is red-proven: the concurrent-writer race test and the entry-level typed-`/reset` test (entering through `initSessionState`, not the inner function) each fail against the pre-fix code exactly as observed live and pass after.

Live validation on a v2026.6.10 production deployment (session ids redacted):

```
typed /reset:
  <sid-A>.jsonl.reset.2026-07-11T16-45-15.346Z
  <sid-A>.trajectory.jsonl.reset.2026-07-11T16-45-15.346Z
  <sid-A>.trajectory-path.json.reset.2026-07-11T16-45-15.346Z

dashboard delete: same trio shape with .deleted.<ts>, session key removed, clean re-mint on next message

typed /new with OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR set (trajectory lives outside the sessions dir):
  sessions dir:  <sid-B>.jsonl.reset.<ts>  +  <sid-B>.trajectory-path.json.reset.<ts>
  external dir:  <sid-B>.jsonl.reset.<ts>   (renamed in place, same timestamp)
```

## Scope notes

- `applySessionEntryLifecycleMutation` (the batched background-maintenance mutation used by the session reaper, cleanup service, and heartbeat runner) is deliberately not touched: its removed-session cleanup already routes through the trajectory-coupled maintenance helpers, and unreferenced pairs are reclaimed by the age-based prune, which is the correct model for background reaping (no user action to timestamp-couple to).
- [#94593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94593) partially overlaps on intent (reset-time preservation) but implements it in the shared reset-archive helper; this PR covers the delete lifecycle and the typed-command rollover door. If #94593 lands first we are happy to rebase and drop any overlap, and vice versa.

## User Impact

Deleting or resetting a session, from any surface, now leaves a complete archived trio with one shared timestamp instead of orphaned or destroyed trajectory files. Post-incident forensics of tool calls survives resets. Existing retention behavior and bounds are unchanged.

target.title: fix(clawrouter): guard usage snapshot fetch against SSRF redirects
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClawRouter usage snapshot fetches used an unguarded `fetch` against an operator-configured `baseUrl`. A malicious or compromised usage endpoint could redirect the request onto a private/internal address, and the call path skipped the shared SSRF guard already used for ClawRouter live catalog discovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route `fetchClawRouterUsage` through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` the same way live catalog discovery does: the guard owns production transport (no caller `fetchImpl`), so DNS pinning cannot be overwritten by provider usage proxy wrappers. Tests inject an optional `fetchGuard` seam; production callers no longer pass `ctx.fetchFn`.

## User Impact

ClawRouter `/usage` status no longer follows redirects from the configured host into private/internal networks. Healthy public ClawRouter usage endpoints continue to work.

## Evidence

### Unit + controlled-server production-transport proof

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ ... > maps the managed monthly budget and usage totals 151ms
 ✓ ... > shows aggregate usage for an unmetered key 2ms
 ✓ ... > does not expose an upstream error body 1ms
 ✓ ... > bounds successful usage response bodies 17ms
 ✓ ... > fetches usage through the production SSRF-guarded transport 326ms
 ✓ ... > blocks private-network redirects on the production transport path 55ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 5.62s
```

The last two cases exercise production `fetchClawRouterUsage` with no injected fetch/guard: a real `node:http` loopback server for healthy usage, and a `302` to `http://10.0.0.1:9/v1/usage` that the shared guard rejects before a second hop.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** ClawRouter usage fetches no longer follow redirects from the configured host onto private/internal targets, and production transport stays under the shared SSRF guard's dispatcher.
- **Canonical reachability path:** provider usage snapshot → `fetchUsageSnapshot` in `extensions/clawrouter/index.ts` → `fetchClawRouterUsage` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` (no `fetchImpl`).
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime SSRF guard; controlled `node:http` server on loopback; private redirect target.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + `ssrfPolicyFromHttpBaseUrlAllowedHostname` already used by ClawRouter live catalog discovery; same guard-owned transport shape as catalog (no provider usage proxy as `fetchImpl`).
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with real HTTP listeners.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ |extensions| extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts > ClawRouter usage > fetches usage through the production SSRF-guarded transport 326ms
 ✓ |extensions| extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts > ClawRouter usage > blocks private-network redirects on the production transport path 55ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 5.62s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Healthy usage returns the mapped snapshot over the guard-owned transport; private-network redirect rejects with a blocked/private/internal error and the controlled server sees only the first hop.
- **What was not tested:** Live ClawRouter cloud `/v1/usage` against a real proxy key; Gateway status UI end-to-end; HTTP_PROXY-managed usage routing (usage now matches catalog and uses guard-owned direct transport rather than `resolveProxyFetchFromEnv` as `fetchImpl`).
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. Only the ClawRouter usage HTTP transport gains the shared SSRF guard with guard-owned dispatcher. Successful responses from the configured host are unchanged; operator-configured private base URLs remain allowed when that hostname is the configured endpoint (same policy shape as catalog discovery). Usage snapshot fetching no longer routes through the provider usage proxy fetch wrapper, matching catalog discovery.

target.body:
Closes #103758

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where LINE groups configured with `requireMention: true` could not require a mention before non-text messages (image/video/audio/file) reached the agent. Any photo, video, voice clip, or file posted in such a group was always processed, regardless of whether the bot was actually mentioned, because LINE's Messaging API never attaches mention metadata to non-text messages and the mention-gate logic could not account for that.

Fixes an issue where operators of mention-gated LINE groups would see the bot react to every image/video/audio/file dropped in the chat, even when nobody addressed the bot, when they expected the same "must be mentioned" behavior that already applies to text messages (per #34438 / #35847).

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds two new **opt-in** LINE group config fields — `requireMentionForNonText` and `pendingMediaLimit` — so operators can explicitly turn on mention gating for non-text messages without changing default behavior for anyone else. Because LINE never reports a mention on the non-text message itself, a bounded per-group pending-media queue (default limit 3) retains the most recent skipped media until a later message in the same group is mentioned and fully processed, at which point the queued media is attached to that turn and the queue is cleared. This lets a user post a photo, then follow up with `@bot look at this`, and have the photo still reach the agent.

A prior attempt at the opt-in flag alone (#68197) went stale without merging and did not include the retention queue, which meant skipped media was simply dropped forever once a group opted in — this PR keeps the same opt-in, default-false posture that maintainers asked for on #68197, and adds the missing retention piece on top.

## User Impact

LINE operators can now set `channels.line.accounts.<id>.groups.<groupId>.requireMentionForNonText: true` (alongside `requireMention: true`) to require an `@mention` before non-text messages reach the agent, matching the existing text-message behavior. Skipped media isn't lost — up to `pendingMediaLimit` (default 3) recent items are retained per group and delivered alongside the next mentioned message. Existing configs are unaffected since both fields default to off/unset.

## Evidence

`pnpm test:extension line` — 26 test files, **313 tests passing** (up from 307 on `main`; +6 in `bot-handlers.test.ts`, +2 in `config-schema.test.ts`):

```

```

New tests cover:

- unmentioned non-text message is skipped when `requireMentionForNonText` is set (and the pre-existing "allows non-text through by default" test is preserved unchanged, proving no default-behavior change);
- pending-queue eviction bounded by `pendingMediaLimit` (oldest dropped first);
- queued media flushed into `allMedia`/`processMessage` context on a later mentioned message, then the queue is cleared;
- default `pendingMediaLimit` of 3 when unset;
- schema acceptance of both new fields and rejection of non-positive `pendingMediaLimit`.

## Summary

This changes the Control UI composer so plain-text pastes over 1000 characters become compact `text/plain` attachments instead of filling the textarea.

The attachment uses the existing chat attachment payload path. When the user sends it, the chat request includes the pasted text as a file attachment with `mimeType: "text/plain"`; when the user clicks “Show in text field”, the attachment is removed and the full paste is restored into the composer draft as normal message text.

- Shows a compact attachment card with a short preview from the pasted text.
- Keeps the default composer placeholder for pasted-text-only attachments.

- Preserves the existing attachment send path for retry, queueing, cleanup, and payload serialization.

target.title: fix(web): apply Control UI text size to content typography
target.body:
## Summary

In this PR, the Appearance text-size setting applies across Control UI content typography instead of only affecting the chat transcript. Shared content font sizes now route through `--control-ui-text-scale`, while touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing 16px minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not reintroduce mobile Safari focus zoom.

## Screenshots

Settings at the default M text size, showing the Appearance text-size control in English.

![Settings text size at M](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-settings-text-size-m-en.png)

Overview at XXL text size, showing the larger page typography across cards and form controls.

![Overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-overview-xxl-en.png)

Channels at XXL text size, showing the larger channel cards and actions.

![Channels using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-channels-xxl-en.png)

Mobile Overview at XXL text size, showing the narrow layout with scaled content typography.

![Mobile overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-mobile-overview-xxl-en.png)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Appearance text-size setting so it affects Control UI content typography beyond the chat transcript. Before this PR, the setting could be saved while many Settings, quick settings, overview, channel, session, skill, and content surfaces still used fixed font sizes.

## Why This Change Was Made

In this PR, shared Control UI font sizes route through the existing `--control-ui-text-scale` value instead of hard-coded pixel sizes. The change keeps layout chrome and spacing stable while letting readable content, forms, cards, chat text, composer text, and page typography respond to S/M/L/XL/XXL.

Touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing `--control-ui-input-text-size` minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not shrink mobile inputs below 16px and reintroduce Safari focus zoom.

## User Impact

Changing Text size in Appearance now produces visible typography changes across the main product surfaces, while M remains the normal/default size.

## Validation

- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMRTUXB | tr '\n' ' ')`

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
